decisions.choice: make: a command to dig the ditches
alternatives: This wadi will be made full of pools
decisions.reason: The verb form can give a command or simply describe what will happen. Read as a command, the kings must dig ditches to hold the water Yahweh will send (verse 17). Read as a description, Yahweh himself says he will make the wadi full of pools. The command fits the instructions that follow, but the other reading is possible.

decisions.choice: ditches, ditches: many ditches
decisions.reason: Repeating a word shows a great number: the wadi is to be full of them.

decisions.choice: wadi: a valley or streambed dry for most of the year
decisions.reason: A wadi carries water only after rain. The army is camped in or near one on the border of Moab.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / The LORD says this / This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: The messenger formula, worded at each level as in these books.

decisions.choice: streambed / dry streambed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the wadi (m3). Literal keeps the word "wadi".

decisions.choice: torrente (Literal); cauce (Balanced); cauce seco (Readable)
decisions.reason: Spanish "torrente" is the word for a stream that runs only in the rains; Balanced and Readable describe the wadi as a streambed, dry for most of the year (m3).

decisions.choice: "ce torrent" (L); "ce lit de torrent" (B); "ce lit de rivière à sec" (R)
decisions.reason: The wadi is a valley that runs with water only in the rainy season; "torrent" is the usual French word for it in Bible geography, and Readable says plainly that it is dry.

decisions.choice: "bonde" (Literal); "bonde la kijito" (Balanced); "bonde la kijito kilichokauka" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no everyday word for a wadi; "bonde" (valley) at Literal, with the stream bed added at Balanced and its dryness at Readable.

decisions.choice: "thung lũng khe" (L); "lòng khe" (B); "lòng khe cạn" (R)
decisions.reason: A wadi is a streambed dry most of the year (m3); "khe" is the Vietnamese word for such a gully, as in "khe Xết-rôn".

decisions.choice: The messenger formula in 하오체 ("말씀하시오"), as Elisha speaks to the kings in this scene; God's words in single quotes keep 해라체
decisions.reason: The formula follows the speech level Elisha uses with the kings (verse 13), and God's own words keep his plain style.

decisions.choice: ribeiro (L); leito de riacho (B); leito seco de riacho (R); valas, valas (L), vala após vala (B)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the wadi (m3) is "ribeiro" at Literal, the word 1 Kings 2:37 uses in Portuguese for a seasonal streambed, and Balanced and Readable describe it, "leito de riacho" and "leito seco de riacho", as 1 Samuel 17:40 does in Portuguese; "uádi" is unknown to most Brazilian readers. Literal keeps the doubled "valas, valas" (m2); Balanced says "vala após vala".

source.text: כִּֽי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לֹֽא־תִרְא֥וּ ר֨וּחַ֙ וְלֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ גֶ֔שֶׁם וְהַנַּ֥חַל הַה֖וּא יִמָּ֣לֵא מָ֑יִם וּשְׁתִיתֶ֛ם אַתֶּ֥ם וּמִקְנֵיכֶ֖ם וּֽבְהֶמְתְּכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh, not you will see wind and not you will see rain, and the wadi the that will be filled [with] water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your animals.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'You will not see wind, and you will not see rain, yet that wadi will be filled [with] water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your animals.'
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'You will see no wind and no rain, yet that streambed will fill with water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your pack animals.'
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'You will not feel any wind or see any rain. Yet that streambed will fill with water. Then you and your cattle and your other animals will have water to drink.'

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “No {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} viento ni {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} lluvia, y ese torrente se llenará de agua, y {{plural_you:beberán ustedes|beberéis vosotros}} y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} ganado y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} animales”.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: “No {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} viento ni lluvia, pero ese cauce se llenará de agua, y {{plural_you:beberán ustedes|beberéis vosotros}}, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} ganado y {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} bestias de carga”.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “No {{plural_you:sentirán|sentiréis}} viento ni {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} lluvia. Aun así, ese cauce se llenará de agua. Entonces {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} ganado y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} otros animales {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} agua para beber”.

fr.L: Car ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : “Vous ne verrez pas de vent et vous ne verrez pas de pluie, et ce torrent se remplira d’eau, et vous boirez, vous, votre bétail et vos bêtes.”
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : “Vous ne verrez ni vent ni pluie, et pourtant ce lit de torrent se remplira d’eau, et vous boirez, vous, votre bétail et vos bêtes de somme.”
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : “Vous ne sentirez pas de vent et vous ne verrez pas de pluie. Pourtant ce lit de rivière se remplira d’eau. Alors vous aurez de l’eau à boire, pour vous, pour vos troupeaux et pour vos autres animaux.”

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: 'Hamtaona upepo, wala hamtaona mvua, lakini bonde lile litajaa maji, nanyi mtakunywa, ninyi na mifugo yenu na wanyama wenu.'
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: 'Hamtaona upepo wala mvua, lakini bonde lile la kijito litajaa maji, nanyi mtakunywa, ninyi na mifugo yenu na wanyama wenu wa kubeba mizigo.'
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: 'Hamtahisi upepo wala kuona mvua. Hata hivyo bonde lile la kijito litajaa maji. Ndipo ninyi na ng'ombe wenu na wanyama wenu wengine mtapata maji ya kunywa.'

vi.L: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: 'Các ngươi sẽ không thấy gió, không thấy mưa, nhưng thung lũng khe ấy sẽ đầy nước, và các ngươi sẽ uống, các ngươi cùng gia súc và thú vật của các ngươi.'
vi.B: Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: 'Các ngươi sẽ không thấy gió, cũng không thấy mưa, nhưng lòng khe ấy sẽ đầy nước, và các ngươi cùng gia súc và thú chở hàng của các ngươi sẽ được uống.'
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: 'Các ngươi sẽ không thấy có gió hay mưa. Thế nhưng lòng khe ấy sẽ đầy nước. Các ngươi cùng bò và các thú vật khác của các ngươi sẽ có nước uống.'

ko.L: 왜냐하면 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하시기 때문이오. '너희가 바람을 보지 못하고 비를 보지 못할 것이나, 그 골짜기가 물로 가득 찰 것이니, 너희와 너희 가축과 너희 짐승들이 마실 것이다.'
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하시오. '너희는 바람도 보지 못하고 비도 보지 못할 것이다. 그래도 그 골짜기에 물이 가득 차서, 너희와 너희 가축과 너희 짐승들이 마실 것이다.'
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀은 이것이오. '너희는 바람 한 점 느끼지 못하고, 비 한 방울 보지 못할 것이다. 그래도 그 골짜기에는 물이 가득 찰 것이다. 그러면 너희와 너희 소와 다른 짐승들이 마실 물이 생길 것이다.'

pt.L: Pois assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: 'Vocês não verão vento, e não verão chuva, mas aquele ribeiro se encherá [de] água, e vocês beberão, vocês e o seu gado e os seus animais.'
pt.B: Pois assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: 'Vocês não verão vento nem chuva, mas aquele leito de riacho se encherá de água, e vocês beberão, vocês, o seu gado e os seus animais de carga.'
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: 'Vocês não vão sentir vento nem ver chuva. Mesmo assim, aquele leito de riacho vai se encher de água. Então vocês, o seu gado e os seus outros animais vão ter água para beber.'

decisions.choice: no wind and no rain, yet water: Yahweh's own gift
decisions.reason: Wind and rain would come before a storm. The water will come without any sign of a storm where they are, so that they know it is Yahweh's doing.

decisions.choice: your livestock and your animals: the herds and the beasts of burden
decisions.reason: The first word names livestock kept as property, herds and flocks taken along for food; the second names animals in general, here the pack animals of verse 9.

decisions.choice: pack animals / other animals
decisions.reason: Balanced names the animals of verse 9 that carried the army's loads; Readable keeps it general.

decisions.choice: feel any wind
decisions.reason: Readable says "feel" for wind, which cannot be seen. Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's single verb "see".

source.text: וְנָקַ֥ל זֹ֖את בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְנָתַ֥ן אֶת־מוֹאָ֖ב בְּיֶדְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it is light this in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and he will give Moab into your hand.

en.L: And this is a light thing in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give Moab into your hand.
en.B: This is only a small thing in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will also hand Moab over to you.
en.R: And this is easy for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to do. He will also let you defeat Moab.

es.L: Y esto es cosa ligera a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entregará a Moab en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} mano.
es.B: Esto es poca cosa a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} también entregará a Moab en {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} manos.
es.R: Y esto es fácil de hacer para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. También hará que {{plural_you:ustedes derroten|vosotros derrotéis}} a Moab.

fr.L: Et c’est peu de chose aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} livrera Moab entre vos mains.
fr.B: Et ce n’est encore qu’une petite chose aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} livrera aussi Moab entre vos mains.
fr.R: Et c’est facile pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Il vous fera aussi vaincre Moab.

sw.L: Na hili ni jambo jepesi machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atamtia Moabu mkononi mwenu.
sw.B: Hili ni jambo dogo tu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atawatia Wamoabu mikononi mwenu pia.
sw.R: Na hili ni rahisi kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kulifanya. Pia atawawezesha kuwashinda Wamoabu.

vi.L: Điều này là việc nhỏ trước mắt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ phó Mô-áp vào tay các vua.
vi.B: Đây chỉ là một việc nhỏ trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng sẽ phó Mô-áp vào tay các vua.
vi.R: Việc này thật dễ đối với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ngài cũng sẽ cho các vua đánh bại Mô-áp.

ko.L: 그리고 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈에 가벼운 일이오. 그가 모압을 당신들의 손에 넘겨주실 것이오.
ko.B: 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 보시기에 하찮은 일이오. 그분께서는 모압도 당신들의 손에 넘겨주실 것이오.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께는 이 일이 아주 쉬운 일이오. 그분께서는 당신들이 모압도 이기게 해 주실 것이오.

pt.L: E isto [é] pouca coisa aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} entregará Moabe na mão de vocês.
pt.B: Isso é pouca coisa aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} também entregará Moabe a vocês.
pt.R: E isso é fácil para {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} fazer. Ele também vai deixar vocês derrotarem Moabe.

decisions.choice: a light thing in the eyes of Yahweh: easy for Yahweh
decisions.reason: "Light" means of little weight. Giving water in the desert is a small thing for Yahweh; he will do more.

decisions.choice: he will give Moab into your hand: the answer to the king's fear
decisions.reason: Jehoram feared that Yahweh would give the three kings into the hand of Moab (verses 10, 13). Yahweh will give Moab into theirs instead.

decisions.choice: hand Moab over to you / let you defeat Moab
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Balanced and Readable say what "give into your hand" means.

decisions.choice: "naye" with the deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Swahili carries "he" in the verb prefix, which cannot be capitalised, so the span goes on the joined pronoun "naye" ("and he"), as the style guide allows; Readable has no free pronoun and no span.

decisions.choice: Elisha calls the three kings "các vua"
decisions.reason: The prophet addresses the kings as kings, as he calls the king of Israel "vua" (verse 13).

decisions.choice: "당신들의 손" for the plural "your hand": Elisha now speaks to all three kings
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here is plural; Korean marks the plural so that the promise is to the three kings together.

source.text: וְהִכִּיתֶ֞ם כָּל־עִ֤יר מִבְצָר֙ וְכָל־עִ֣יר מִבְח֔וֹר וְכָל־עֵ֥ץ טוֹב֙ תַּפִּ֔ילוּ וְכָל־מַעְיְנֵי־מַ֖יִם תִּסְתֹּ֑מוּ וְכֹל֙ הַחֶלְקָ֣ה הַטּוֹבָ֔ה תַּכְאִ֖בוּ בָּאֲבָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will strike every city of fortification and every city of choice, and every tree good you will fell, and all springs of water you will stop up, and every portion the good you will ruin with stones.

en.L: And you will strike every fortified city and every choice city, and every good tree you will fell, and all the springs of water you will stop up, and every good plot [of land] you will ruin with stones."
en.B: You will strike down every fortified town and every major town. You will cut down every good tree, block every spring of water, and ruin every good field with stones."
en.R: You will conquer every town with walls and every important town. You will cut down every good tree, block up every spring, and ruin every good field by covering it with stones."

es.L: Y {{plural_you:herirán|heriréis}} toda ciudad fortificada y toda ciudad escogida, y todo árbol bueno {{plural_you:talarán|talaréis}}, y todos los manantiales de agua {{plural_you:cegarán|cegaréis}}, y toda parcela buena {{plural_you:arruinarán|arruinaréis}} con piedras».
es.B: {{plural_you:Destruirán|Destruiréis}} toda ciudad fortificada y toda ciudad importante. {{plural_you:Talarán|Talaréis}} todo árbol bueno, {{plural_you:cegarán|cegaréis}} todos los manantiales y {{plural_you:arruinarán|arruinaréis}} con piedras todo campo fértil».
es.R: {{plural_you:Conquistarán|Conquistaréis}} toda ciudad con murallas y toda ciudad importante. {{plural_you:Talarán|Talaréis}} todo árbol bueno, {{plural_you:taparán|taparéis}} todos los manantiales y {{plural_you:arruinarán|arruinaréis}} todo campo fértil cubriéndolo de piedras».

fr.L: Et vous frapperez toute ville fortifiée et toute ville de choix, et tout bon arbre vous abattrez, et toutes les sources d’eau vous boucherez, et toute bonne parcelle vous ruinerez avec des pierres. »
fr.B: Vous frapperez toutes les villes fortifiées et toutes les villes importantes. Vous abattrez tous les bons arbres, vous boucherez toutes les sources et vous ruinerez tous les bons champs en les couvrant de pierres. »
fr.R: Vous prendrez toutes les villes qui ont des remparts et toutes les villes importantes. Vous couperez tous les bons arbres, vous boucherez toutes les sources, et vous abîmerez tous les bons champs en les couvrant de pierres. »

sw.L: Nanyi mtapiga kila mji wenye ngome na kila mji bora, na kila mti mzuri mtaukata, na chemchemi zote za maji mtaziziba, na kila shamba zuri mtaliharibu kwa mawe."
sw.B: Mtashinda kila mji wenye ngome na kila mji mkubwa. Mtaukata kila mti mzuri, mtaziba kila chemchemi ya maji, na kuharibu kila shamba zuri kwa mawe."
sw.R: Mtateka kila mji wenye kuta na kila mji muhimu. Mtaukata kila mti mzuri, mtaziba kila chemchemi, na kuharibu kila shamba zuri kwa kulifunika kwa mawe."

vi.L: Các vua sẽ đánh phá mọi thành kiên cố và mọi thành tốt nhất, sẽ đốn mọi cây tốt, lấp mọi nguồn nước, và lấy đá phá hỏng mọi thửa đất tốt."
vi.B: Các vua sẽ đánh chiếm mọi thành kiên cố và mọi thành quan trọng. Các vua sẽ đốn mọi cây tốt, lấp mọi nguồn nước, và lấy đá phá hỏng mọi ruộng đất tốt."
vi.R: Các vua sẽ chiếm mọi thành có tường lũy và mọi thành quan trọng. Các vua sẽ đốn mọi cây tốt, lấp mọi mạch nước, và lấy đá phủ lên mọi ruộng tốt để làm hư hại chúng."

ko.L: 그리고 당신들은 모든 견고한 성읍과 모든 좋은 성읍을 치고, 모든 좋은 나무를 베고, 모든 물의 샘들을 막고, 모든 좋은 땅을 돌로 망칠 것이오."
ko.B: 당신들은 요새화된 성읍과 중요한 성읍을 모두 치고, 좋은 나무를 모두 베고, 샘을 모두 막고, 좋은 밭을 모두 돌로 덮어 못 쓰게 만들 것이오."
ko.R: 당신들은 성벽이 있는 성읍과 중요한 성읍을 모두 정복할 것이오. 좋은 나무는 모두 베어 버리고, 샘은 모두 막아 버리고, 좋은 밭은 모두 돌로 덮어 못 쓰게 만들 것이오."

pt.L: E vocês ferirão toda cidade fortificada e toda cidade escolhida, e toda árvore boa vocês derrubarão, e todas as fontes de água vocês taparão, e todo bom pedaço [de terra] vocês arruinarão com pedras."
pt.B: Vocês vão derrotar todas as cidades fortificadas e todas as cidades importantes. Vão cortar todas as árvores boas, tapar todas as fontes de água e arruinar com pedras todos os campos bons."
pt.R: Vocês vão conquistar todas as cidades que têm muralhas e todas as cidades importantes. Vão cortar todas as árvores boas, tapar todas as fontes e arruinar todos os campos bons, cobrindo-os de pedras."

decisions.choice: fortified city ... choice city: every strong and every important town
decisions.reason: The two phrases sound alike in Hebrew. A "choice" city is a fine or leading one. Together they mean all the towns that mattered.

decisions.choice: you will strike ... fell ... stop up ... ruin: a prediction that also directs
decisions.reason: The verbs say what the army will do. Coming from Yahweh's prophet, they also tell the kings what to do (verse 25).

decisions.choice: every good tree you will fell: total ruin of the land
decisions.reason: Cutting the trees, stopping the springs and covering the fields with stones would leave Moab unable to support its people for years. The law forbade cutting down fruit trees while besieging a city (Deuteronomy 20:19-20). The text does not say how the prophet's word relates to that law.

decisions.choice: major town / town with walls; important town
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "fortified" and "choice" in common words (m1).

decisions.choice: field
decisions.reason: The word means a portion or plot of land; Balanced and Readable say "field", the cultivated land the stones would spoil.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ כַּעֲל֣וֹת הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְהִנֵּה־מַ֥יִם בָּאִ֖ים מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ אֱד֑וֹם וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ אֶת־הַמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the morning, as went up the offering, and look, water coming from [the] way of Edom, and was filled the land [with] the water.

en.L: And it was in the morning, at the going up of the offering, and look, water was coming from the way of Edom, and the land was filled [with] the water.
en.B: The next morning, about the time of the morning offering, water suddenly came flowing from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
en.R: The next morning, at the time when the morning sacrifice was offered, water suddenly came flowing from the direction of Edom. Soon the whole area was full of water.

es.L: Y sucedió por la mañana, cuando se ofrecía la ofrenda, que he aquí venían aguas por el camino de Edom, y la tierra se llenó de agua.
es.B: A la mañana siguiente, a la hora de la ofrenda de la mañana, de pronto vino agua de la dirección de Edom, y la tierra se llenó de agua.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, a la hora en que se ofrecía el sacrificio de la mañana, de pronto empezó a llegar agua desde la dirección de Edom. Pronto toda la zona quedó llena de agua.

fr.L: Et il arriva le matin, à l’heure où l’on monte l’offrande, que voici, de l’eau arrivait par le chemin d’Édom, et le pays fut rempli d’eau.
fr.B: Le lendemain matin, vers l’heure de l’offrande du matin, l’eau arriva soudain de la direction d’Édom, et le pays fut rempli d’eau.
fr.R: Le lendemain matin, à l’heure où l’on présentait le sacrifice du matin, l’eau est soudain arrivée de la direction d’Édom. Bientôt, toute la région a été pleine d’eau.

sw.L: Ikawa asubuhi, wakati wa kupanda kwa sadaka, na tazama, maji yakaja kutoka njia ya Edomu, nayo nchi ikajaa maji.
sw.B: Asubuhi iliyofuata, karibu na wakati wa sadaka ya asubuhi, ghafula maji yakaja yakitiririka kutoka upande wa Edomu, nayo nchi ikajaa maji.
sw.R: Asubuhi iliyofuata, wakati sadaka ya asubuhi ilipotolewa, ghafula maji yakaja yakitiririka kutoka upande wa Edomu. Punde eneo lote likajaa maji.

vi.L: Sáng hôm sau, vào lúc dâng tế lễ, kìa, nước từ phía Ê-đôm chảy đến, và đất đầy nước.
vi.B: Sáng hôm sau, vào khoảng giờ dâng tế lễ buổi sáng, bỗng nhiên nước từ phía Ê-đôm chảy đến, và cả vùng ngập nước.
vi.R: Sáng hôm sau, vào giờ dâng sinh tế buổi sáng, bỗng nhiên nước từ phía Ê-đôm chảy tràn đến. Chẳng bao lâu cả vùng đầy nước.

ko.L: 그리고 아침에 제물을 드릴 때에, 보라, 에돔 쪽 길에서 물이 흘러왔고, 땅이 물로 가득 찼다.
ko.B: 이튿날 아침 제물을 드릴 무렵에, 갑자기 에돔 쪽에서 물이 흘러와 온 땅에 물이 가득 찼다.
ko.R: 이튿날 아침 제물을 드리는 시간이 되자, 갑자기 에돔 쪽에서 물이 흘러 내려왔다. 곧 그 일대가 온통 물로 가득 찼다.

pt.L: E aconteceu, de manhã, na hora de se oferecer a oferta, que eis que vinha água pelo caminho de Edom, e a terra se encheu da água.
pt.B: Na manhã seguinte, por volta da hora da oferta da manhã, de repente veio água correndo da direção de Edom, e a terra se encheu de água.
pt.R: Na manhã seguinte, na hora em que se oferecia o sacrifício da manhã, de repente começou a vir água correndo da direção de Edom. Logo toda a região ficou cheia de água.

decisions.choice: as the offering went up: at the time of the regular morning offering
decisions.reason: The offering named here was the daily one made at the temple in the morning (Exodus 29:38-42). Elijah's prayer on Mount Carmel came at the time of the evening offering (1 Kings 18:36). The time ties Yahweh's answer to the hour of worship.

decisions.choice: water coming from the way of Edom: water flowing down from the south
decisions.reason: Rain on the high ground of Edom can send a sudden flood down dry valleys far away, where no storm is seen. The text presents the water as Yahweh's promised gift (verse 17).

decisions.choice: look: a sudden sight
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to something seen suddenly, from the point of view of those who saw it.

decisions.choice: the morning offering / the morning sacrifice
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the offering by its time (m1), as 1 Kings 18:29 and 36 name the evening offering.

decisions.choice: The next morning
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that this was the morning after Elisha spoke.

source.text: וְכָל־מוֹאָב֙ שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּֽי־עָל֥וּ הַמְּלָכִ֖ים לְהִלָּ֣חֶם בָּ֑ם וַיִּצָּעֲק֗וּ מִכֹּ֨ל חֹגֵ֤ר חֲגֹרָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ עַֽל־הַגְּבֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And all Moab had heard that had come up the kings to fight against them, and they were called out, from all girding a belt and upward, and they stood at the border.

en.L: And all Moab had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, and they were called out, from all who could put on a belt and upward, and they took their stand at the border.
en.B: Meanwhile all Moab had heard that the kings had come to fight against them. Everyone old enough to put on a sword belt, and older, was called out, and they took up positions at the border.
en.R: By now all the Moabites had heard that the kings had come to fight against them. So every man old enough to fight, young and old, was called up. They went and stood ready at the border.

es.L: Y todo Moab había oído que los reyes habían subido a pelear contra ellos, y fueron convocados, desde todos los que podían ceñirse el cinturón en adelante, y se pusieron en la frontera.
es.B: Mientras tanto, todo Moab había oído que los reyes venían a pelear contra ellos. Convocaron a todos los que tenían edad para ceñirse la espada, y aun a los mayores, y tomaron posiciones en la frontera.
es.R: Para entonces todos los moabitas sabían que los reyes venían a pelear contra ellos. Así que llamaron a todos los hombres en edad de luchar, jóvenes y viejos. Fueron a la frontera y se quedaron allí listos para la batalla.

fr.L: Et tout Moab avait appris que les rois étaient montés pour combattre contre eux, et ils furent convoqués, depuis tous ceux qui pouvaient ceindre la ceinture et au-dessus, et ils se tinrent à la frontière.
fr.B: Entre-temps, tous les Moabites avaient appris que les rois étaient venus les attaquer. Tous les hommes en âge de ceindre l’épée, et au-delà, furent convoqués, et ils prirent position à la frontière.
fr.R: Pendant ce temps, tous les Moabites avaient appris que les rois étaient venus les attaquer. Alors on a appelé tous les hommes en âge de se battre, jeunes et vieux. Ils sont allés se tenir prêts à la frontière.

sw.L: Moabu wote walikuwa wamesikia kwamba wafalme wamepanda kupigana nao, nao wakaitwa, tangu wote wawezao kujifunga mshipi na zaidi, wakasimama mpakani.
sw.B: Wakati huo Wamoabu wote walikuwa wamesikia kwamba wafalme wamekuja kupigana nao. Kila mtu aliyefikia umri wa kujifunga mshipi wa upanga, na wazee zaidi, aliitwa, nao wakashika nafasi zao mpakani.
sw.R: Wakati huo Wamoabu wote walikuwa wamesikia kwamba wafalme wamekuja kupigana nao. Basi kila mwanamume aliyeweza kupigana, vijana kwa wazee, aliitwa. Wakaenda, wakasimama tayari mpakani.

vi.L: Toàn dân Mô-áp đã nghe rằng các vua đã đi lên để đánh họ, nên họ được kêu gọi, từ mọi người có thể thắt đai lưng trở lên, và họ đứng ở biên giới.
vi.B: Bấy giờ toàn dân Mô-áp đã nghe tin các vua kéo đến đánh họ. Mọi người đủ tuổi đeo gươm trở lên đều được gọi nhập ngũ, và họ dàn quân ở biên giới.
vi.R: Lúc ấy toàn dân Mô-áp đã nghe tin các vua đến đánh họ. Vì vậy mọi người đàn ông đủ tuổi cầm vũ khí, trẻ cũng như già, đều được gọi ra trận. Họ đến đứng sẵn sàng ở biên giới.

ko.L: 그리고 온 모압이 왕들이 자기들과 싸우러 올라왔다는 것을 들었고, 허리띠를 띨 수 있는 모든 사람과 그 이상[의 사람들이] 소집되어, 그들이 국경에 섰다.
ko.B: 그 사이에 온 모압은 왕들이 자기들을 치러 올라왔다는 소식을 들었다. 그래서 칼을 찰 나이가 된 사람부터 그 위로 모두 소집되어 국경에 진을 쳤다.
ko.R: 그때쯤 모압 사람들은 모두 왕들이 자기들과 싸우러 왔다는 소식을 들었다. 그래서 싸울 수 있는 나이의 남자는 젊은이부터 늙은이까지 모두 불려 나왔다. 그들은 국경으로 가서 싸울 준비를 하고 섰다.

pt.L: E todo o Moabe tinha ouvido que os reis tinham subido para lutar contra eles, e foram convocados, desde todos os que podiam cingir um cinto e daí para cima, e se posicionaram na fronteira.
pt.B: Enquanto isso, todos os moabitas tinham ouvido que os reis tinham vindo lutar contra eles. Todos os que tinham idade para pôr o cinto da espada, e os mais velhos também, foram convocados e tomaram posição na fronteira.
pt.R: A essa altura, todos os moabitas já tinham ouvido que os reis tinham vindo lutar contra eles. Por isso, todos os homens com idade para lutar, jovens e velhos, foram convocados. Eles foram e ficaram prontos na fronteira.

decisions.choice: had heard: before the water came
decisions.reason: The verb form looks back. While the allied army was marching, Moab had already gathered its men.

decisions.choice: all girding a belt and upward: every man old enough to bear arms
decisions.reason: A soldier put on a belt to carry his sword. "And upward" means everyone of that age and older.

decisions.choice: they were called out: summoned to war
decisions.reason: The verb means to cry out; in this form it means to be summoned by a call to arms (Judges 6:34-35).

decisions.choice: sword belt / old enough to fight
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the belt was for; Readable says what the idiom means (m2).

decisions.choice: "칼을 찰 나이가 된 사람" at Balanced for "all who could put on a belt"
decisions.reason: As the English Balanced "sword belt": the belt is the soldier's belt, and the idiom means every man of fighting age (m2). Literal keeps the belt.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ זָרְחָ֣ה עַל־הַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּרְא֨וּ מוֹאָ֥ב מִנֶּ֛גֶד אֶת־הַמַּ֖יִם אֲדֻמִּ֥ים כַּדָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they rose early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water, and saw Moab from opposite the water red like blood.

en.L: And they rose early in the morning, and the sun had risen on the water, and Moab saw the water opposite [them] red like blood.
en.B: Early in the morning they got up, and the sun was shining on the water. To the Moabites facing it, the water looked as red as blood.
en.R: Early the next morning, when the Moabites got up, the sun was shining on the water. From where they stood, the water looked red like blood.

es.L: Y se levantaron temprano por la mañana, y el sol brilló sobre las aguas, y vio Moab enfrente las aguas rojas como sangre.
es.B: Muy de mañana se levantaron, y el sol brillaba sobre el agua. A los moabitas, que la miraban de frente, el agua les pareció roja como la sangre.
es.R: Temprano a la mañana siguiente, cuando los moabitas se levantaron, el sol brillaba sobre el agua. Desde donde estaban, el agua parecía roja como la sangre.

fr.L: Et ils se levèrent de bon matin, et le soleil brillait sur les eaux, et Moab vit en face [d’eux] les eaux rouges comme du sang.
fr.B: Ils se levèrent de bon matin, et le soleil brillait sur l’eau. Aux Moabites qui la voyaient en face, l’eau parut rouge comme du sang.
fr.R: Le lendemain, quand les Moabites se sont levés de bon matin, le soleil brillait sur l’eau. De là où ils étaient, l’eau semblait rouge comme du sang.

sw.L: Wakaamka asubuhi na mapema, na jua lilikuwa limechomoza juu ya maji, nao Moabu wakayaona maji yaliyokuwa mbele [yao] mekundu kama damu.
sw.B: Asubuhi na mapema waliamka, na jua lilikuwa likiangaza juu ya maji. Kwa Wamoabu waliokuwa wakiyaelekea, maji yalionekana mekundu kama damu.
sw.R: Asubuhi na mapema siku iliyofuata, Wamoabu walipoamka, jua lilikuwa likiangaza juu ya maji. Kutoka pale walipokuwa, maji yalionekana mekundu kama damu.

vi.L: Họ dậy sớm vào buổi sáng, và mặt trời đã chiếu trên mặt nước, và Mô-áp thấy nước ở phía đối diện đỏ như máu.
vi.B: Sáng sớm họ thức dậy thì mặt trời đang chiếu trên mặt nước. Người Mô-áp nhìn từ phía đối diện thì thấy nước đỏ như máu.
vi.R: Sáng sớm hôm sau, khi người Mô-áp thức dậy, mặt trời đang chiếu trên mặt nước. Từ chỗ họ đứng, nước trông đỏ như máu.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 아침 일찍 일어났는데, 해가 물 위에 떠올랐고, 모압이 맞은편의 물이 피처럼 붉은 것을 보았다.
ko.B: 그들이 아침 일찍 일어났을 때에 해가 물 위를 비추고 있었다. 모압 사람들이 맞은편에서 보니, 그 물이 피처럼 붉었다.
ko.R: 이튿날 아침 일찍 모압 사람들이 일어났을 때에 해가 물을 비추고 있었다. 그들이 서 있는 곳에서 보니, 물이 피처럼 붉었다.

pt.L: E eles se levantaram cedo de manhã, e o sol tinha nascido sobre a água, e Moabe viu de frente a água vermelha como sangue.
pt.B: De manhã cedo eles se levantaram, e o sol brilhava sobre a água. Para os moabitas, que estavam de frente para ela, a água parecia vermelha como sangue.
pt.R: Na manhã seguinte, bem cedo, quando os moabitas se levantaram, o sol estava brilhando sobre a água. De onde eles estavam, a água parecia vermelha como sangue.

decisions.choice: Moab ... red like blood: a play on the name Edom
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, "Edom", "red" and "blood" sound alike. The water came from Edom (verse 20) and looked red to Moab, which led the Moabites to think of blood.

decisions.choice: the sun shone on the water: the early light made it look red
decisions.reason: The low morning sun, perhaps with red earth in the water, gave it a red color seen from a distance. The Moabites did not know that water had come (verse 17).

decisions.choice: saw ... from opposite: saw it from a distance, facing it
decisions.reason: The Moabites saw the water from their positions across from the allied camp.

decisions.choice: looked as red as blood
decisions.reason: Balanced says the water "looked" red, since the Moabites were wrong about what they saw (verse 23).

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ דָּ֣ם זֶ֔ה הָחֳרֵ֤ב נֶֽחֶרְבוּ֙ הַמְּלָכִ֔ים וַיַּכּ֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְעַתָּ֥ה לַשָּׁלָ֖ל מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, blood [is] this; surely have fought each other the kings, and they have struck each his neighbor; and now, to the plunder, Moab!

en.L: And they said, "This [is] blood! The kings have surely fought each other, and they have struck each other down. And now, to the plunder, Moab!"
en.B: They said, "This is blood! The kings must have fought one another and killed each other. Now, Moab, to the plunder!"
en.R: They said, "That is blood! The kings must have turned on each other and killed one another. Come on, Moabites! Let us go and take everything they have!"

es.L: Y dijeron: «¡Esto [es] sangre! Ciertamente los reyes han peleado entre sí, y se han matado unos a otros. ¡Ahora, al botín, Moab!».
es.B: Dijeron: «¡Es sangre! Los reyes deben de haber peleado entre sí y se han matado unos a otros. ¡Ahora, Moab, al botín!».
es.R: Dijeron: «¡Eso es sangre! Los reyes deben de haberse peleado y se han matado unos a otros. ¡Vamos, moabitas! ¡Vamos a quitarles todo lo que tienen!».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « C’est du sang ! Les rois se sont certainement battus entre eux, et ils se sont frappés l’un l’autre. Et maintenant, au butin, Moab ! »
fr.B: Ils dirent : « C’est du sang ! Les rois ont dû se battre et s’entretuer. Maintenant, Moab, au pillage ! »
fr.R: Ils ont dit : « C’est du sang ! Les rois ont dû se battre entre eux et s’entretuer. Allez, Moabites ! Allons prendre tout ce qu’ils ont ! »

sw.L: Wakasema, "Hii [ni] damu! Hakika wafalme wamepigana wao kwa wao, wameuana kila mtu na mwenzake. Basi sasa, kwenye nyara, Moabu!"
sw.B: Wakasema, "Hii ni damu! Lazima wafalme wamepigana wao kwa wao na kuuana. Sasa, Moabu, twendeni tukateke nyara!"
sw.R: Wakasema, "Hiyo ni damu! Lazima wafalme wamegeukiana na kuuana. Haya, Wamoabu! Twendeni tukachukue kila kitu walicho nacho!"

vi.L: Họ nói: "Đây là máu! Các vua chắc chắn đã đánh nhau và giết hại lẫn nhau. Bây giờ, hãy đi cướp lấy, hỡi Mô-áp!"
vi.B: Họ nói: "Máu đấy! Các vua hẳn đã đánh nhau và giết lẫn nhau rồi. Hỡi Mô-áp, bây giờ hãy đi cướp chiến lợi phẩm!"
vi.R: Họ nói: "Máu đấy! Các vua hẳn đã quay ra đánh nhau và giết lẫn nhau rồi. Nào, anh em Mô-áp! Chúng ta hãy đi lấy hết của cải của chúng!"

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 말했다. "이것은 피[다]! 왕들이 분명히 서로 싸워서 서로 쳐 죽였다. 그러니 이제 모압아, 노략하러 가자!"
ko.B: 그들이 말했다. "이것은 피다! 왕들이 서로 싸워서 서로 죽였음이 틀림없다. 모압아, 이제 노략하러 가자!"
ko.R: 그들이 말했다. "저것은 피다! 왕들이 서로 등을 돌려 싸우다가 서로 죽인 게 틀림없다. 자, 모압 사람들아! 가서 그들의 물건을 모두 빼앗자!"

pt.L: E disseram: "Isto [é] sangue! Os reis certamente lutaram entre si, e se feriram uns aos outros. E agora, ao saque, Moabe!"
pt.B: Eles disseram: "Isto é sangue! Os reis devem ter lutado entre si e se matado uns aos outros. Agora, Moabe, ao saque!"
pt.R: Eles disseram: "Aquilo é sangue! Os reis devem ter brigado entre si e matado uns aos outros. Vamos, moabitas! Vamos pegar tudo o que eles têm!"

decisions.choice: have surely fought each other: the kings must have turned their swords on each other
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for sword, and it is doubled for emphasis. The Moabites are sure of what they think they see.

decisions.choice: the kings have struck each other: allies falling out
decisions.reason: An alliance of rival kingdoms could break apart in a quarrel (Judges 7:22; 1 Samuel 14:20). The Moabites think this has happened.

decisions.choice: each his neighbor: one another
decisions.reason: "Each ... his neighbor" is the Hebrew way of saying "one another".

decisions.choice: to the plunder, Moab!: a call to go and seize the spoil
decisions.reason: Moab is addressed as one army. Plunder was what an army took from a defeated enemy's camp.

decisions.choice: Come on, Moabites! Let us go and take everything they have!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the short cry into plain sentences that say what it calls for (m4).

source.text: וַיָּבֹאוּ֮ אֶל־מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיָּקֻ֤מוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּ אֶת־מוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּכּוּ־בָ֔הּ וְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to [the] camp of Israel, and rose up Israel and struck Moab, and they fled from before them; and they struck in it, and striking Moab.

en.L: And they came to the camp of Israel, and Israel rose up and struck Moab, and they fled before them; and they struck in it, striking Moab.
en.B: But when the Moabites reached the camp of Israel, the Israelites sprang up and attacked them, and they fled. The Israelites pushed on into the land, striking down the Moabites.
en.R: But when the Moabites came to Israel's camp, the Israelites jumped up and attacked them, and the Moabites ran away. The Israelites chased them into their own land and kept on killing them.

es.L: Y llegaron al campamento de Israel, y se levantó Israel e hirió a Moab, y huyeron delante de ellos; y entraron en ella hiriendo a Moab.
es.B: Pero cuando los moabitas llegaron al campamento de Israel, los israelitas se levantaron y los atacaron, y ellos huyeron. Los israelitas avanzaron por su tierra, matando a los moabitas.
es.R: Pero cuando los moabitas llegaron al campamento de Israel, los israelitas se levantaron de un salto y los atacaron, y los moabitas salieron huyendo. Los israelitas los persiguieron hasta su propia tierra y siguieron matándolos.

fr.L: Et ils arrivèrent au camp d’Israël, et Israël se leva et frappa Moab, et ils s’enfuirent devant eux ; et ils frappèrent dans le pays, frappant Moab.
fr.B: Mais quand les Moabites atteignirent le camp d’Israël, les Israélites se levèrent et les attaquèrent, et ils s’enfuirent devant eux. Les Israélites pénétrèrent dans le pays en battant les Moabites.
fr.R: Mais quand les Moabites sont arrivés au camp d’Israël, les Israélites se sont levés d’un bond et les ont attaqués, et les Moabites se sont enfuis. Les Israélites les ont poursuivis jusque dans leur pays et ont continué à les tuer.

sw.L: Wakaja kwenye kambi ya Israeli, nao Israeli wakainuka, wakawapiga Moabu, nao wakakimbia mbele yao; wakaingia ndani yake, wakiwapiga Moabu.
sw.B: Lakini Wamoabu walipofika kwenye kambi ya Israeli, Waisraeli waliinuka ghafula, wakawashambulia, nao wakakimbia. Waisraeli wakaingia ndani ya nchi, wakiwaua Wamoabu.
sw.R: Lakini Wamoabu walipofika kwenye kambi ya Israeli, Waisraeli waliruka juu, wakawashambulia, nao Wamoabu wakakimbia. Waisraeli wakawafukuza mpaka ndani ya nchi yao wenyewe, wakaendelea kuwaua.

vi.L: Họ đến trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên, và Y-sơ-ra-ên đứng dậy đánh Mô-áp, và chúng chạy trốn trước mặt họ; họ tiến vào trong xứ, đánh giết Mô-áp.
vi.B: Nhưng khi người Mô-áp đến trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên, quân Y-sơ-ra-ên vùng dậy tấn công, và quân Mô-áp bỏ chạy. Quân Y-sơ-ra-ên tiến vào trong xứ, đánh giết người Mô-áp.
vi.R: Nhưng khi người Mô-áp đến trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên, quân Y-sơ-ra-ên liền vùng dậy tấn công, và người Mô-áp bỏ chạy. Quân Y-sơ-ra-ên đuổi theo họ vào tận xứ của họ và tiếp tục chém giết.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 이스라엘 진영에 이르렀을 때에, 이스라엘이 일어나 모압을 쳤고, 그들이 그들 앞에서 도망쳤다. 그리고 그들이 그 안으로 쳐들어가며 모압을 쳤다.
ko.B: 그러나 모압 사람들이 이스라엘 진영에 이르자, 이스라엘 사람들이 일어나 그들을 쳤다. 모압 사람들은 도망쳤고, 이스라엘 사람들은 그 땅으로 쳐들어가며 모압 사람들을 쳐 죽였다.
ko.R: 그러나 모압 사람들이 이스라엘 진영에 왔을 때에, 이스라엘 사람들이 벌떡 일어나 그들을 공격했다. 모압 사람들은 도망쳤다. 이스라엘 사람들은 그들을 뒤쫓아 모압 땅까지 들어가며 계속 죽였다.

pt.L: E chegaram ao acampamento de Israel, e Israel se levantou e feriu Moabe, e eles fugiram diante deles; e feriram nela, ferindo Moabe.
pt.B: Mas, quando os moabitas chegaram ao acampamento de Israel, os israelitas se levantaram e os atacaram, e eles fugiram. Os israelitas avançaram pela terra, matando os moabitas.
pt.R: Mas, quando os moabitas chegaram ao acampamento de Israel, os israelitas se levantaram de repente e os atacaram, e os moabitas fugiram. Os israelitas os perseguiram até dentro da terra deles e continuaram matando-os.

decisions.choice: they struck in it: Israel pressed on into Moab's land, striking the Moabites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text, as its vowels read it, says "they struck in it", that is, Israel fought on inside Moab. The written letters can also be read "they went into it", and the ancient Greek translation has "they went in". Either way Israel advanced into Moab, cutting down the Moabites as it went.

decisions.choice: and striking Moab: striking them as they went
decisions.reason: The verb form without a subject describes the action that went with the advance.

decisions.choice: Israel: the allied army
decisions.reason: "Israel" here names the whole army in Israel's camp, Judah's and Edom's men with it.

decisions.choice: into the land / into their own land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "it" refers to: the land of Moab.

source.text: וְהֶעָרִ֣ים יַהֲרֹ֡סוּ וְכָל־חֶלְקָ֣ה ט֠וֹבָה יַשְׁלִ֨יכוּ אִישׁ־אַבְנ֜וֹ וּמִלְא֗וּהָ וְכָל־מַעְיַן־מַ֤יִם יִסְתֹּ֨מוּ֙ וְכָל־עֵֽץ־ט֣וֹב יַפִּ֔ילוּ עַד־הִשְׁאִ֧יר אֲבָנֶ֛יהָ בַּקִּ֖יר חֲרָ֑שֶׂת וַיָּסֹ֥בּוּ הַקַּלָּעִ֖ים וַיַּכּֽוּהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the cities they tore down, and every good portion they threw each his stone and filled it, and every spring of water they stopped up, and every good tree they felled, until he left its stones in Kir-hareseth; and went around the slingers and struck it.

en.L: And they tore down the cities, and on every good plot [of land] each threw his stone, and they filled it, and they stopped up every spring of water, and they felled every good tree, until only its stones were left in Kir-hareseth; and the slingers surrounded [it] and struck it.
en.B: They tore down the towns, and each man threw a stone on every good field until it was covered. They blocked every spring of water and cut down every good tree. At last only Kir-hareseth was left with its stones standing, and the slingers surrounded it and attacked it.
en.R: They destroyed the towns. Every soldier threw a stone onto each good field until the fields were covered. They blocked up every spring and cut down every good tree. In the end only the walls of Kir-hareseth were still standing. But soldiers with slings surrounded that city and attacked it.

es.L: Y derribaron las ciudades, y en toda parcela buena echó cada uno su piedra, y la llenaron; y cegaron todo manantial de agua y talaron todo árbol bueno, hasta que solo quedaron sus piedras en Kir-hareset; y los honderos [la] rodearon y la atacaron.
es.B: Derribaron las ciudades, y cada hombre echó una piedra en todo campo fértil hasta cubrirlo. Cegaron todos los manantiales y talaron todos los árboles buenos. Al final solo quedó Kir-hareset con sus piedras en pie, y los honderos la rodearon y la atacaron.
es.R: Destruyeron las ciudades. Cada soldado echaba una piedra en cada campo fértil hasta que los campos quedaron cubiertos. Taparon todos los manantiales y talaron todos los árboles buenos. Al final solo quedaban en pie las murallas de Kir-hareset. Pero soldados armados con hondas rodearon esa ciudad y la atacaron.

fr.L: Et ils détruisirent les villes, et sur toute bonne parcelle chacun jeta sa pierre, et ils la remplirent, et ils bouchèrent toute source d’eau, et ils abattirent tout bon arbre, jusqu’à ne laisser [debout] que ses pierres à Qir-Haréseth ; et les frondeurs l’entourèrent et la frappèrent.
fr.B: Ils démolirent les villes, et chacun jeta une pierre sur tous les bons champs jusqu’à les couvrir. Ils bouchèrent toutes les sources et abattirent tous les bons arbres. À la fin, il ne resta que Qir-Haréseth avec ses murailles de pierre ; les frondeurs l’encerclèrent et l’attaquèrent.
fr.R: Ils ont détruit les villes. Chaque soldat a jeté une pierre sur chaque bon champ, jusqu’à ce que les champs soient couverts. Ils ont bouché toutes les sources et coupé tous les bons arbres. À la fin, seuls les murs de Qir-Haréseth étaient encore debout. Mais des soldats armés de frondes ont encerclé cette ville et l’ont attaquée.

sw.L: Wakaibomoa miji, na juu ya kila shamba zuri kila mtu akatupa jiwe lake, wakalijaza, wakaziziba kila chemchemi ya maji, wakaukata kila mti mzuri, mpaka mawe yake tu yakabaki katika Kir-haresethi; nao wapiga kombeo wakauzunguka, wakaupiga.
sw.B: Wakaibomoa miji, na kila mtu akatupa jiwe juu ya kila shamba zuri mpaka likafunikwa. Wakaziba kila chemchemi ya maji na kukata kila mti mzuri. Mwishowe Kir-haresethi tu ndio uliobaki na mawe yake yamesimama, nao wapiga kombeo wakauzunguka, wakaushambulia.
sw.R: Waliiharibu miji. Kila askari alitupa jiwe juu ya kila shamba zuri mpaka mashamba yakafunikwa. Waliziba kila chemchemi na kukata kila mti mzuri. Mwishowe kuta za Kir-haresethi peke yake ndizo zilizobaki zimesimama. Lakini askari wenye kombeo waliuzunguka mji huo, wakaushambulia.

vi.L: Họ phá đổ các thành, và trên mọi thửa đất tốt mỗi người ném đá của mình vào cho đến khi lấp đầy; họ lấp mọi nguồn nước và đốn mọi cây tốt, cho đến khi chỉ còn lại đá của nó ở Kiệt Ha-rê-sết; rồi những người bắn ná vây quanh và đánh nó.
vi.B: Họ phá đổ các thành, và mỗi người ném một hòn đá lên mọi ruộng đất tốt cho đến khi phủ kín. Họ lấp mọi nguồn nước và đốn mọi cây tốt. Cuối cùng chỉ còn lại Kiệt Ha-rê-sết với những bức tường đá, và những người bắn ná vây quanh thành ấy mà tấn công.
vi.R: Họ phá hủy các thành. Mỗi người lính ném đá lên từng ruộng tốt cho đến khi phủ kín cả ruộng. Họ lấp mọi mạch nước và đốn mọi cây tốt. Cuối cùng chỉ còn tường thành Kiệt Ha-rê-sết là còn đứng vững. Nhưng những người lính cầm ná vây quanh thành ấy và tấn công.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 성읍들을 허물었고, 모든 좋은 땅에 각자 자기 돌을 던져 그것을 메웠으며, 모든 물의 샘을 막고 모든 좋은 나무를 베어, 마침내 길하레셋에 그 돌들만 남았다. 그리고 물매꾼들이 [그곳을] 둘러싸고 그곳을 쳤다.
ko.B: 그들은 성읍들을 허물고, 좋은 밭마다 각자 돌을 던져 그 밭을 가득 덮었다. 샘을 모두 막고 좋은 나무를 모두 베었다. 마침내 길하레셋만 돌로 쌓은 성벽이 서 있는 채로 남았는데, 물매꾼들이 그 성을 에워싸고 공격했다.
ko.R: 그들은 성읍들을 무너뜨렸다. 군인들은 저마다 좋은 밭에 돌을 던져서 밭을 돌로 덮어 버렸다. 샘을 모두 막고 좋은 나무를 모두 베었다. 마침내 길하레셋 성의 성벽만 남았다. 그러나 물매를 든 군인들이 그 성을 둘러싸고 공격했다.

pt.L: E derrubaram as cidades, e em todo bom pedaço [de terra] cada um lançou a sua pedra, e o encheram, e taparam toda fonte de água, e derrubaram toda árvore boa, até que [só] restaram as suas pedras em Quir-Haresete; e os atiradores de funda [a] cercaram e a feriram.
pt.B: Eles derrubaram as cidades, e cada homem jogou uma pedra em cada campo bom, até cobri-lo. Taparam todas as fontes de água e cortaram todas as árvores boas. Por fim só restou Quir-Haresete, com as suas pedras de pé, e os atiradores de funda a cercaram e a atacaram.
pt.R: Eles destruíram as cidades. Cada soldado jogava uma pedra em cada campo bom, até que os campos ficaram cobertos. Taparam todas as fontes e cortaram todas as árvores boas. No fim, só as muralhas de Quir-Haresete continuavam de pé. Mas soldados armados com fundas cercaram aquela cidade e a atacaram.

decisions.choice: towns, fields, springs, trees: Elisha's word carried out
decisions.reason: The army does each of the things Elisha said it would (verse 19), in a different order.

decisions.choice: until he left its stones in Kir-hareseth: until only Kir-hareseth stood
alternatives: until only the stones of Kir-hareseth were left
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and hard: literally "until he left its stones in Kir-hareseth". It most likely means that nothing was left standing except the stone walls of Kir-hareseth. Kir-hareseth was Moab's chief stronghold (Isaiah 16:7, 11).

decisions.choice: the slingers: soldiers armed with slings
decisions.reason: A sling threw stones with great force and could reach defenders on a wall (Judges 20:16).

decisions.choice: until only its stones were left
decisions.reason: Literal gives the impersonal "he left" as a passive, since no person is meant (m2).

decisions.choice: the walls of Kir-hareseth
decisions.reason: Readable says what "its stones" refers to, the city's stone walls (m2).

decisions.choice: "Kiệt Ha-rê-sết"
decisions.reason: The Moabite city in the usual Vietnamese form, kept for Kir-hareseth wherever it appears.

decisions.choice: "길하레셋" for Kir-hareseth and "물매꾼들" (L, B), "물매를 든 군인들" (R) for the slingers
decisions.reason: "물매" is the familiar Korean word for the sling (as David's in 1 Samuel 17); the place name follows the usual Protestant form.

decisions.choice: Quir-Haresete; os atiradores de funda (L, B), soldados armados com fundas (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the city (m2) is written as one name with a hyphen and the final "-e" Portuguese adds after a consonant, as "Quir-Haresete". The slingers (m3) are "atiradores de funda", the plain words, rather than the rare "fundibulários"; "funda" is the word of David's sling in 1 Samuel 17:40 and of Judges 20:16 in Portuguese.

source.text: וַיַּרְא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֔ב כִּֽי־חָזַ֥ק מִמֶּ֖נּוּ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֣ח א֠וֹתוֹ שְׁבַע־מֵא֨וֹת אִ֜ישׁ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֗רֶב לְהַבְקִ֛יעַ אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ אֱד֖וֹם וְלֹ֥א יָכֹֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] king of Moab that was too strong for him the battle, and he took with him seven hundred men drawing sword, to break through to [the] king of Edom; and not they were able.

en.L: And the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, and he took with him 700 men who drew the sword, to break through to the king of Edom; but they were not able.
en.B: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was going against him, he took with him 700 swordsmen to try to break through to the king of Edom, but they failed.
en.R: The king of Moab saw that he was losing the battle. So he took 700 soldiers armed with swords and tried to break through the enemy lines to reach the king of Edom. But they could not get through.

es.L: Y vio el rey de Moab que la batalla era más fuerte que él, y tomó consigo setecientos hombres que sacaban espada, para abrirse paso hasta el rey de Edom; pero no pudieron.
es.B: Cuando el rey de Moab vio que la batalla se le ponía en contra, tomó consigo setecientos hombres armados de espada para intentar abrirse paso hasta el rey de Edom, pero no lo lograron.
es.R: El rey de Moab vio que estaba perdiendo la batalla. Entonces tomó setecientos soldados armados con espadas e intentó romper las filas enemigas para llegar hasta el rey de Edom. Pero no pudieron pasar.

fr.L: Et le roi de Moab vit que la bataille était trop forte pour lui, et il prit avec lui 700 hommes tirant l’épée, pour percer jusqu’au roi d’Édom ; mais ils ne le purent pas.
fr.B: Quand le roi de Moab vit que la bataille tournait contre lui, il prit avec lui 700 hommes armés d’épées pour tenter de percer jusqu’au roi d’Édom, mais ils échouèrent.
fr.R: Le roi de Moab a vu qu’il était en train de perdre la bataille. Alors il a pris 700 soldats armés d’épées et il a essayé de traverser les lignes ennemies pour atteindre le roi d’Édom. Mais ils n’ont pas pu passer.

sw.L: Mfalme wa Moabu akaona kwamba vita vimemzidi nguvu, akachukua pamoja naye watu 700 wenye kufuta upanga, ili wapenye kwa mfalme wa Edomu; lakini hawakuweza.
sw.B: Mfalme wa Moabu alipoona kwamba vita vinamwendea vibaya, alichukua pamoja naye wapiga upanga 700 ili wajaribu kupenya mpaka kwa mfalme wa Edomu, lakini walishindwa.
sw.R: Mfalme wa Moabu aliona kwamba anashindwa vitani. Basi akachukua askari 700 wenye panga, akajaribu kupenya katikati ya majeshi ya adui ili amfikie mfalme wa Edomu. Lakini hawakuweza kupita.

vi.L: Vua Mô-áp thấy trận chiến quá mạnh đối với mình, nên đem theo 700 người cầm gươm để phá vòng vây đến chỗ vua Ê-đôm; nhưng họ không thể làm được.
vi.B: Khi vua Mô-áp thấy mình sắp thua trận, vua dẫn theo 700 kiếm sĩ cố phá vòng vây để tiến đến chỗ vua Ê-đôm, nhưng không được.
vi.R: Vua Mô-áp thấy mình đang thua trận. Vì vậy vua dẫn 700 binh lính cầm gươm cố chọc thủng phòng tuyến của địch để đến chỗ vua Ê-đôm. Nhưng họ không vượt qua được.

ko.L: 그리고 모압 왕이 전쟁이 자기에게 너무 강한 것을 보고, 칼을 빼는 사람 700명을 데리고 에돔 왕에게로 뚫고 나가려고 했으나, 그들이 할 수 없었다.
ko.B: 모압 왕은 싸움이 자기에게 불리하게 돌아가는 것을 보고, 칼을 쓰는 군사 700명을 데리고 에돔 왕 쪽으로 뚫고 나가려 했으나 실패했다.
ko.R: 모압 왕은 자기가 싸움에서 지고 있다는 것을 알았다. 그래서 칼을 든 군인 700명을 데리고 적의 진을 뚫고 에돔 왕에게까지 가려고 했다. 그러나 그들은 뚫고 나가지 못했다.

pt.L: E o rei de Moabe viu que a batalha era forte demais para ele, e tomou consigo setecentos homens que puxavam espada, para romper até o rei de Edom; mas não conseguiram.
pt.B: Quando o rei de Moabe viu que a batalha estava se voltando contra ele, levou consigo setecentos homens armados de espada para tentar romper as linhas até o rei de Edom, mas não conseguiram.
pt.R: O rei de Moabe viu que estava perdendo a batalha. Então ele levou setecentos soldados armados com espadas e tentou romper as linhas inimigas para chegar ao rei de Edom. Mas eles não conseguiram passar.

decisions.choice: the battle was too strong for him: he was losing
decisions.reason: The phrase means that the fighting had gone beyond what the king could hold.

decisions.choice: to break through to the king of Edom: to attack where the allies were weakest
decisions.reason: The text does not say why Mesha chose Edom's position. It may have been the weakest part of the siege lines, or he may have hoped that Edom, the least willing ally, would give way.

decisions.choice: men drawing sword: armed fighting men
decisions.reason: "Drawing the sword" describes men able to fight with a sword (Judges 8:10).

decisions.choice: through the enemy lines
decisions.reason: Readable says what Mesha tried to break through.

source.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֶת־בְּנ֨וֹ הַבְּכ֜וֹר אֲשֶׁר־יִמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֗יו וַיַּעֲלֵ֤הוּ עֹלָה֙ עַל־הַ֣חֹמָ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י קֶצֶף־גָּד֖וֹל עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he took his son the firstborn who would reign in his place, and he offered him up [as] a burnt offering on the wall; and was great wrath against Israel, and they set out from against him and returned to the land.

en.L: And he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him up [as] a burnt offering on the wall. And there was great wrath against Israel, and they set out from against him and returned to [their] land.
en.B: Then he took his firstborn son, who was to become king after him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. And great wrath came against Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.
en.R: Then the king of Moab took his oldest son, the one who was to be king after him, and sacrificed him as a burnt offering on top of the city wall. Great anger came against Israel. So the Israelites left the king of Moab and went back to their own land.

es.L: Y tomó a su hijo primogénito, que había de reinar en su lugar, y lo ofreció [en] holocausto sobre la muralla. Y hubo gran ira contra Israel, y se retiraron de él y volvieron a [su] tierra.
es.B: Entonces tomó a su hijo primogénito, el que había de reinar después de él, y lo ofreció en holocausto sobre la muralla. Y vino una gran ira contra Israel, así que se retiraron de allí y volvieron a su tierra.
es.R: Entonces el rey de Moab tomó a su hijo mayor, el que iba a ser rey después de él, y lo sacrificó como holocausto encima de la muralla de la ciudad. Vino una gran ira contra Israel. Así que los israelitas dejaron al rey de Moab y regresaron a su tierra.

fr.L: Et il prit son fils premier-né, qui devait régner à sa place, et il l’offrit [en] holocauste sur la muraille. Et il y eut une grande colère contre Israël, et ils s’éloignèrent de lui et retournèrent dans [leur] pays.
fr.B: Alors il prit son fils aîné, qui devait devenir roi après lui, et il l’offrit en holocauste sur la muraille. Et une grande colère vint sur Israël, si bien que les Israélites s’éloignèrent de lui et retournèrent dans leur pays.
fr.R: Alors le roi de Moab a pris son fils aîné, celui qui devait être roi après lui, et il l’a offert en sacrifice, brûlé sur le haut de la muraille de la ville. Une grande colère est venue contre Israël. Alors les Israélites ont laissé le roi de Moab et sont rentrés dans leur pays.

sw.L: Akamchukua mwanawe mzaliwa wa kwanza, ambaye angetawala mahali pake, akamtoa [kuwa] sadaka ya kuteketezwa juu ya ukuta. Kukawa na ghadhabu kuu juu ya Israeli, nao wakaondoka kutoka kwake, wakarudi [katika] nchi [yao].
sw.B: Kisha akamchukua mwanawe mzaliwa wa kwanza, ambaye angekuwa mfalme baada yake, akamtoa kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa juu ya ukuta. Ndipo ghadhabu kuu ikaja juu ya Israeli, nao wakaondoka kutoka kwake, wakarudi katika nchi yao wenyewe.
sw.R: Kisha mfalme wa Moabu akamchukua mwanawe wa kwanza, yule ambaye angekuwa mfalme baada yake, akamtoa kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa juu ya ukuta wa mji. Hasira kubwa ikaja juu ya Israeli. Basi Waisraeli wakamwacha mfalme wa Moabu, wakarudi katika nchi yao wenyewe.

vi.L: Vua bắt con trai đầu lòng của mình, là người sẽ làm vua thay mình, và dâng nó làm của lễ thiêu trên tường thành. Và có cơn thịnh nộ lớn giáng trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, và họ rút đi khỏi vua ấy và trở về xứ [mình].
vi.B: Bấy giờ vua bắt con trai đầu lòng, là người sẽ kế vị mình, dâng làm của lễ thiêu trên tường thành. Cơn thịnh nộ lớn giáng trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, nên họ rút quân khỏi vua ấy và trở về xứ mình.
vi.R: Bấy giờ vua Mô-áp bắt con trai trưởng, là người sẽ làm vua sau mình, đem dâng làm của lễ thiêu trên tường thành. Một cơn giận dữ lớn giáng trên Y-sơ-ra-ên. Vì vậy quân Y-sơ-ra-ên bỏ vua Mô-áp mà rút về xứ mình.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 자기를 대신하여 왕이 될 맏아들을 데려다가 성벽 위에서 그를 번제[로] 드렸다. 그러자 이스라엘에게 큰 진노가 있었고, 그들이 그에게서 떠나 [자기] 땅으로 돌아갔다.
ko.B: 그러자 그는 자기 뒤를 이어 왕이 될 맏아들을 데려다가 성벽 위에서 번제물로 바쳤다. 그러자 이스라엘에게 큰 진노가 임했고, 그들은 그에게서 물러나 자기 땅으로 돌아갔다.
ko.R: 그러자 모압 왕은 자기 뒤를 이어 왕이 될 큰아들을 데려다가 성벽 위에서 번제물로 바쳤다. 그러자 큰 분노가 이스라엘에게 내렸다. 그래서 이스라엘 사람들은 모압 왕을 두고 물러나 자기 땅으로 돌아갔다.

pt.L: E ele tomou o seu filho primogênito, que havia de reinar em seu lugar, e o ofereceu [como] holocausto sobre a muralha. E houve grande ira contra Israel, e partiram de junto dele e voltaram para a [sua] terra.
pt.B: Então ele tomou o seu filho primogênito, que seria rei depois dele, e o ofereceu como holocausto sobre a muralha. E veio uma grande ira contra Israel; por isso eles se retiraram de lá e voltaram para a sua terra.
pt.R: Então o rei de Moabe pegou o seu filho mais velho, aquele que seria rei depois dele, e o sacrificou como holocausto em cima da muralha da cidade. Uma grande ira veio contra Israel. Por isso os israelitas deixaram o rei de Moabe e voltaram para a sua terra.

decisions.choice: he offered his firstborn son as a burnt offering on the wall: a human sacrifice in sight of the besiegers
decisions.reason: Mesha offered the heir to his throne, most likely to Chemosh, the god of Moab (1 Kings 11:7), in a last plea for help. He did it on the city wall, where the armies outside could see it. The law of Israel condemned such sacrifices (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31).

decisions.choice: there was great wrath against Israel: whose wrath is not said
alternatives: the Moabites' fury rose against Israel
decisions.reason: The word for wrath is used most often of God's anger (Numbers 1:53; 18:5; Joshua 22:20). Here the text does not say whose wrath it was. It may be Yahweh's anger against Israel, perhaps for driving Mesha to this act or for going beyond what Yahweh had said; it may be the fury of the Moabites, roused by the sacrifice; or it may be that Israel was struck with horror and dismay. The writer does not suggest that Chemosh had power. Israel's withdrawal follows directly.

decisions.choice: they set out from against him: the allies broke off the siege
decisions.reason: "Set out" is used for breaking camp. The allies left Mesha and his city and went home without taking Moab back.

decisions.choice: to the land: to their own land
decisions.reason: "The land" means each army's own country.

decisions.choice: wrath (Literal, Balanced); anger (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the Hebrew open about whose wrath it was (m2). None of them names God or the Moabites.

decisions.choice: oldest son
decisions.reason: Readable says "oldest" for "firstborn" and names the king of Moab for clarity.

decisions.choice: gran ira
decisions.reason: "Ira" at every level leaves open, as the Hebrew does, whose wrath it was (m2); Spanish needs no other word at Readable.

decisions.choice: "cơn thịnh nộ" (L, B); "cơn giận dữ" (R)
decisions.reason: Whose wrath it was is not said (m2), so Vietnamese, like the English, does not name its source.

decisions.choice: "진노" (L, B) and "분노" (R) for the wrath, with no owner named
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says whose wrath is not said; Korean, like the Hebrew, leaves the noun without an owner.

decisions.choice: uma grande ira contra Israel (every level)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "ira" is the word for God's anger in the Pentateuch in Portuguese (Numbers 1:53) and can also be human fury, so like the Hebrew it leaves open whose wrath it was (m2); no level names God or the Moabites. Readable keeps "ira", which is plain enough, where the English Readable says "anger"; "raiva" would point to a human feeling.
